clue.text: In which one might find a god in retreat with Hindus principally inspired?

definitions.text: In which one might find a god in retreat with Hindus principally inspired?

indicators.note: inspired in its literal sense of breathed in, so one piece is taken inside the other
retreating means going backwards, so the god's name is read from right to left

parts.note: Mars is the Roman god of war

indicators.note: principally means in the first place, so only the opening letter of Hindus is used

explanation.surface: A riddle about where you might meet a deity tucked away on retreat, with Hindus as the main inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns MARS into SRAM, after A; 'inspired' then breathes the H from 'Hindus principally' into the middle. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu religious retreat or hermitage is a place where a god might well be found during a time of withdrawal.

clue.text: Sing around a musical group offering regular fare?

indicators.note: around tells us the first word goes round the next pieces

parts.note: to squeal is to inform on someone, as to sing does in criminal slang
R.E.M. is an American rock band

explanation.surface: Singing round a band seems an odd source of everyday food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sing' looks musical but is underworld slang for informing on accomplices; 'around' signals the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper, balanced meal eaten at the usual times is everyday regular fare.

clue.text: Queen in country with leader overlooked by the rest

indicators.text: with leader overlooked by the rest
indicators.note: in a down entry the remaining letters stand above the first one, so the leading letter drops to the bottom

parts.note: Iran is a country in the Middle East

explanation.surface: A queen in some country, whose ruler is ignored by everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with leader overlooked by the rest' sends the I of IRAN from the top to the bottom of the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A rani is a Hindu queen or a rajah's wife, so this is a regional title for a queen.

clue.text: Lawyer in film with pained expression showing profitable instinct?

indicators.note: in puts the lawyer inside the film

parts.note: a mist is a thin film of moisture or haze
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
ouch is what someone says when hurt

explanation.surface: An attorney appearing in a movie wears a pained look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' suggests cinema but here means a thin layer: MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: King Midas turned everything he touched to gold, so the phrase means a knack for making money from anything.

clue.text: Bird from large island tucking into nut

indicators.note: tucking into means the letters are pushed inside the nut

parts.note: a pecan is a kind of nut
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A bird from a big island eating a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelican is a large water bird with a pouched bill.

clue.text: Repellent rule blocking fighter on the way up

indicators.note: blocking means the rule sits in the middle, obstructing the fighter
in a down entry going up means the fighter's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter aircraft

explanation.surface: A repellent regulation stops a fighter climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' turns MIG into GIM; 'blocking' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grim is forbidding and unpleasant, so repellent in the sense of off-putting.

clue.text: Dressing up unfortunately Conservative enters fantasised state

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of regret, roughly unfortunately

indicators.note: enters puts the letter inside the dream

parts.note: a dream is a state of fantasy

explanation.surface: Getting dressed up, sadly a Tory slips into a daydream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the regretful word round, as this is a down light; 'enters' slips the Tory letter in just after the dream's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad cream is a British bottled condiment, a sweeter cousin of mayonnaise, used as a dressing for salad.

clue.text: South African plant wasting a million for the time being

indicators.note: wasting means a letter is squandered and something else takes its place

parts.note: the protea is a flowering shrub native to South Africa, its national flower

explanation.surface: A South African plant squanders a fortune, at least for now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting a million' swaps the A at the end of PROTEA for M.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used in English to mean temporarily, holding a post only until a permanent choice is made.

clue.text: Reserve glass containing bit of rosé — it reduces tension?

parts.note: ice means reserve or coolness of manner

indicators.note: containing means the glass holds the next letter

parts.note: a beaker is a drinking glass or cup

indicators.note: a bit of the word is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Iced wine in a glass with a drop of rosé to ease a tense atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' suggests booking or a substitute, but here means coolness of manner; 'containing' signals the glass holding the letter from 'bit of rosé'.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebreaker is a remark or game that relaxes strangers, easing social strain.

clue.text: Keen Arab in revolution spread Islam, not a set of reforming principles

indicators.note: revolution means turning round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: keen in the sense of sharp or biting, like acid
Ar is an abbreviation of Arab or Arabic

indicators.note: spread means the letters are scattered and rearranged
not means the letter a is left out

parts.note: the article a, as written

explanation.surface: An eager Arab revolutionary spreading Islam without a fixed programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolution' turns ACIDAR into RADICA; 'not a' drops A from ISLAM, and 'spread' rearranges ISLM as LISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Radicalism is a doctrine advocating thorough political or social reform.

clue.text: Relative acceleration shown by former racing driver commonly mentioned

parts.note: a is the physics symbol for acceleration

indicators.note: commonly suggests the dropped-H speech of a Cockney or other non-standard accent, so the name loses its H

parts.note: James Hunt was the 1976 Formula One world champion

explanation.surface: A family member's speed is discussed with a retired motor racer.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the initial H is a hallmark of Cockney London speech, so HUNT becomes UNT.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a parent's sister, a family relation.

clue.text: Something precious about Republican in beginning

indicators.note: about means the gem goes around the letter

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A treasure concerning a Republican, at the start of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ is a seed or origin from which something develops, its beginning.

clue.text: TV phenomenon favoured among sad types

indicators.note: among places the word inside the others

parts.note: a misery is a gloomy, complaining person
in means fashionable or favoured

explanation.surface: A television hit is popular with depressed viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sad types' are gloomy people, each one a misery; 'among' puts the favoured word just after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniseries is a short serial drama on television, a broadcasting format.

clue.text: Very loud paintings backed by journal in gallery? Mass congestion results

indicators.note: backed means the pieces run backwards

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
art means paintings collectively

indicators.note: in puts the journal inside the gallery

parts.note: the ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts, a London gallery
J is the abbreviation for journal
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Loud art and a magazine in a gallery: the crowds create a jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns FFART into TRAFF. The ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts in London; 'in' puts J inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic jam is a blockage of vehicles on a road, an obvious form of congestion.

clue.text: Irresponsible order given to long-haul pilot?

definitions.meaning: describes someone unreliable and untrustworthy, especially in business
a long-distance aviator might be instructed to take off and travel through the dark hours

explanation.definitionFit: A fly-by-night firm is shady and unreliable, apt to vanish with your money overnight.

clue.text: Criminal rents a pub, leading to son's rude quality

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrongly done, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook leases a bar, and the son shows bad manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges RENTSAPUB into ABRUPTNES.
explanation.definitionFit: Abruptness is curtness of manner, bluntness bordering on discourtesy.

clue.text: A German entering legislative body largely of a very wicked nature

indicators.note: entering means the German word goes inside
largely means most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: a house is a legislative chamber, as in the House of Commons
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: A German entering parliament, mostly, is said to be thoroughly evil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A German' is the German word for a, not a person; 'largely' drops the chamber's last letter and 'entering' slips the word in after its first.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinous describes a crime or act that is utterly odious and atrocious.

clue.text: Describing a form of learning in book before period covering hard topics initially

indicators.note: covering means the period wraps around the letter

parts.note: a year is a period of time
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A study method from a textbook in a school year covering difficult subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' places H inside YEAR, after its Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning by rote, memorising word for word, is the kind of study this phrase describes.

clue.text: Leading cleric, nut about religious instruction with master

indicators.note: about means the head surrounds the other letters

parts.note: pate and nut are both informal words for the head
RI is the school abbreviation for religious instruction

explanation.surface: A senior churchman's head is full of religious teaching and a schoolmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nut' is slang for the head, as is PATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A primate is an archbishop or the chief bishop of a province, the senior churchman.

clue.text: Sweep into fine hotel with a posh car, ultimate in grandiosity? I might!

definitions.text: Sweep into fine hotel with a posh car, ultimate in grandiosity? I might!

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
to lash is to sweep or swish violently, as a tail does
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
RR stands for Rolls-Royce, the classic luxury car

indicators.note: ultimate means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Arriving grandly at a smart hotel in a Rolls is exactly what a showy character would do.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer, a British slang name for a flashy show-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Flash Harry is British slang for an ostentatious, flamboyant man, just the type to arrive in such style.

clue.text: Foreign cheese of a sort masking a fixation

indicators.note: masking means hiding the letter from view, so it is dropped

parts.note: feta is a Greek cheese
the article a, as written
the suffix -ish means somewhat or of a sort

explanation.surface: An imported cheese that, after a fashion, hides an obsession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'masking a' hides the A of FETA, leaving FET.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetish is an obsessive interest or fixation on something.

clue.text: Work in Gaza etc shortly depressed person

indicators.note: in places the work inside the region

parts.note: ME is short for the Middle East, which includes Gaza
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Work in the Middle East leaves someone feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: A mope is someone listless and gloomy, a melancholy person.

clue.text: Rush to be covered by private arrangement

indicators.note: covered by means the letters lie concealed within the next words

explanation.surface: A hurry to get something settled in a private deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear is to dash or race along at high speed.

clue.text: Order to go down note containing appeal requiring money

indicators.note: containing means the comment holds the other pieces

parts.note: a note is a brief remark or comment
it is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A judge's sentence written up as a remark, with an appeal costing cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go down' is British slang for being sent to prison; 'appeal' is sex appeal, and 'containing' puts it with the money inside the note.
explanation.definitionFit: A committal order sends someone to prison or hospital, an official ruling to send a person down.

clue.text: Covering a muscle back to front

indicators.note: the last letter is brought from the back to the front

parts.note: pec is short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: A wrap for a muscle worn the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' takes the C at the end of APEC and puts it first.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape is a sleeveless cloak, a garment covering the shoulders.

clue.text: Secure legendary footballer by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound means the name is said aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Bobby Moore captained England to their 1966 World Cup win

explanation.surface: Signing up a footballing great, to hear people tell it.
explanation.definitionFit: To moor a boat is to make it fast with ropes or an anchor.

clue.text: Rugby side with second playing area — part of a commercial approach?

parts.note: Sale Sharks are an English rugby union club
a pitch is a sports field

explanation.surface: A rugby team with a back-up ground making a business pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Sale Sharks are a rugby club from near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: A salesperson's persuasive patter is a key element of marketing a product.

clue.text: Head of hostelry swamped by rubbish in party

indicators.note: swamped by means the letter is engulfed by the word

parts.note: trash means rubbish

indicators.note: head of means the first letter

explanation.surface: A pub landlord buried in junk at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrash is informal British slang for a lively party or celebration.
